recipes.name: Sopa de Fideos
ingredients_raw: coarse salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Place tomatoes, onion, and garlic into a blender; pulse several times to get the mixture moving, then blend until smooth, 30 seconds to 1 minute.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-low heat; stir in fideo pasta. Fry pasta gently, stirring often, until golden brown, 2 to 5 minutes. Remove from heat.
Pour tomato mixture into a large saucepan; stir in chicken broth and noodles. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low and simmer until noodles are tender, 7 to 8 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper; stir in cilantro and cook until warmed through.

raw_recipe.headline: Sopa de Fideos
raw_recipe.description: This recipe for sopa de fideos (tomato soup with crispy pasta) is simple and easy to make at home. Tastes just like the one at Mexican restaurants.

review.reviewBody: Simple fast soup. Use the mexican chicken broth. It is mixed w flavorful spices that makes it very yummy!

Very delicious! I had to work with what I had in my pantry so I used the shell pasta and some elbow pasta instead. I used knorr suiza (added about a teaspoon to the tomatoe mixture) instead of chicken broth. I added chopped potatoes, carrots and celery. When served I added crumbled Mexican cheese and my kids absolutely loved this! Will definitely make it again.

This was so freakin' good! I had a backlog of tomatoes so I used fresh (didn't even peel them) but I did add a can of Ro*tel to add some heat. I didn't add cilantro because we don't like it. Not sure if my chicken broth was canned, carton, or water and chicken bullion... just use what you got and add what you like and don't add what you don't like. The sautéing of the vermicelli is now a new trick to add to my repertoire. Thanks for the recipe!!

i used one whole yellow onion two cloves of garlic one packet of sazón goya and some adobo 2 chicken broth one beef and 5 sprigs of cilantro after those modifications it tasted just like my childhood :)

A little watered down for my liking. I added a small can of tomato sauce which helped. I think next time I would only do 4-5 cups of liquid instead of the 6 that this recipe comes out to & I think that would help a bit too. Maybe even use the roasted diced tomatoes instead of the regular ones. I also added cumin while frying the noodles. This is definitely a good base recipe that can be added to depending on people’s liking.

Very good! I love this soup, but because of heart failure, I'm on a very sodium restrictive diet. So I made exactly as written, but made with 32 oz low-sodium chicken broth,1 tsp no sodium chicken bouillon granules,unsalted diced tomatoes with oregano, basil and garlic, and it was goooood! To the average person it's probably a little bland, but for me it was perfect and I got my soup fix I was craving.

Update: I have since made this recipe several times. I've added a 4 oz can of diced green chilis and definitely use fresh cilantro if you can. Also added 10 oz extra lean ground turkey cooked with Mrs. Dash taco season and added it to the soup. It's a great way to add a little protein to a nice, light soup. This is definitely one of my favorite very low sodium soups on this site.

actually upon going over those ingredients I do a lot differently as far as measurements go .. this soup is superb. 
I use 3 tomatoes, a sliver of white onion (about 1/8 of it), 3 cloves of garlic (or more, I'm a garlic nut) and chicken broth .. blend all of the ingredients and cook it down till it reduces a few times and the flavor marries. Of course salt & pepper to taste. Sometimes I'll add egg noodles but it tastes fine w/o.

Omg my my this is a very good dish! But why did we have to put the pasta in the skillet? I also added jalapeños peppers and a little red pepper flakes also some ground beef ..This is like Spaghetti Tex mex without the beans or cheese! Delish!

We had a nanny from Guatemala, who would make sopa de fideos and I loved it.
My spouse is from Guatemala and can't cook. This is the closest I have come to the soup of my youth. I toast a half teaspoon of cumin seeds with the fideos and add diced jalapenos.

I have to say this was not bad. Made as directed and we liked it but thought it was bland. Nothing wrong w the recipe just our preference of needing more flavor. The next day, I added black beans, peppers, jalapenos, cumin and chili powder and that was wonderful. Thank you for sharing this recipe.

This is very tasty and easy to make. I added a jalapeño to the blender and an extra garlic clove but otherwise followed the recipe. I see it as an excellent appetizer but it’s not hearty enough for my tastes as a main dish. Thanks for a great recipe!

I loved the fideo soup. It reminded me of fideo my grandma used to make. It was easy to make, The hardest part is browning the pasta. I think next time I will leave the onions chunky. I did add some garlic salt, garlic powder and onion powder. I will make the soup again.

We had this for lunch today and enjoyed it. Never had this dish before, but if I make again, I’ll use a can of Del Monte Basil, Garlic & Oregano tomatoes which I think will kick up the flavor even more. I know there are a lot of cilantro haters out there, but I will say that it brought some good flavor to the sopa. Served with some Swiss Cheese and mini saltine crackers.
This recipe is great and it tastes like the authentic Mexican soup as long as you use Knorr's caldo de pollo y tomate. The broth really makes the soup!
Second time making this soup I just Love it.❤️
This was very good. The flavor was yummy.

Soap de fideo is like meatballs in Italy. Every family makes them a little different. I made this recipe twice and it is my favorite. Blending the onions and garlic raw rather than frying them gives the soup a light bright flavor. I add some chicken bouillon or soup base and quite a bit of chili pepper.
This turned out fantastic, very easy to make and has become my favorite college meal!

I had to work with what I had on the shelf. I cut the recipe in half for two using only 1/3 of the bag of fideos. Also, I used fire-roasted tomatoes, added some minced chipotles and topped with chopped avocados. Yum!
Loved it! Easy to make and my whole family enjoyed it! A keeper.
